subject: Brightlyt — rate harmonization & migration economics
messages:
From: Claire Jenkins <cjenkins@brightlyt.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <talvarez@brightlyt.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor economics question — pricing match request

Sean —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We liked Redwood's performance profile and the ability to run across both hosted and private modes — high on our radar as we standardize inference across product.

Before we get deeper, procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a rate harmonization / price-match offer relative to our incumbent (FluxScale). Current terms are: $0.0006/token for gen, $0.0009/token for embeddings, 12-month commit, and a $150k migration credit in year one tied to onboarding milestones.

Two quick asks so procurement can evaluate:
- Can Redwood match/exceed the effective per-token economics (including an equivalent migration assistance credit)?
- If not exact match, what bundle/commit structure would get us within a 10% TCO delta?

I've attached the RFP excerpt (Brightlyt_RFP_2027.pdf) with their pricing schedule. Happy to jump on a quick call this week — Tom (cc'd) is our infra lead and will own evaluation of private deployment feasibility.

Best,
Claire

Claire Jenkins

Claire — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the RFP. Pasted a short answer below and attaching an initial commercial sketch (redwood-offer-v2.xlsx).

Short answer: we can get within the 10% TCO window for most production mixes with a 12-month committed arrangement + a migration assistance structure (combination of upfront credits + onboarding services).

What I need to finalize the exact numbers:
- Typical monthly token volume (or an expected QPS / tokens per month range) — pricing tiers materially change once you cross larger buckets
- Mix of gen vs embeddings (any heavy reranking/embedding index build spikes?)
- Whether you need private on-prem (higher fixed cost) vs hosted + dedicated pool (recommended for hybrid)

Proposed next steps:
1) If you can share an expected 6mo token curve, Marissa and I will produce a tight counter that includes a migration assistance line and a trial credit tied to onboarding milestones.
2) If it looks promising, we'll route a 12-month committed term to give you a stable per-token number and discuss a DocuSign-ready SOW for onboarding.

I've cc'd Marissa (solutions lead) to propose the migration play and typical concessions we include for customers moving from FluxScale.

Thanks — available Wed/Thu afternoons PST for a quick sync.

—Sean

Hi Claire — quick note from our product & solutions side on typical structures we offer for a FluxScale replacement.

We generally combine three levers to hit effective parity:
- Committed baseline rate (12 months) that grants a per-token tier comparable to your incumbent for steady-state traffic.
- Onboarding / migration assistance credit: we can provide a $100k credit applied to invoices across Q1 after launch + 8 hours of priority engineering support for the migration runbook. For larger migrations we layer an additional services SOW.
- Burst / overage protection: fixed overage caps for the first 90 days so you don't see unexpected surges during index rebuilds.

For Brightlyt specifically, given the RFP numbers and typical model mix you described on the call, a 12-month commit in the $1.2M–$2.5M ARR range would let us price gen at ~$0.00055/token and embeddings at ~$0.00085/token after credits (effective).

I attached our migration playbook for reference; it outlines milestones to unlock credits. If you'd like us to try to get within 10% of FluxScale's full-year economics, we can move to a slightly larger onboarding credit and a short-term promotional tier for months 1–3.

Marissa

Sean / Marissa —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the materials. A couple follow-ups from procurement & infra after reviewing your sketch:

1) We can confirm a projected ramp: month1 50M tokens, month2 120M, steady-state ~400M tokens/month by Q4. Gen:embeddings ratio ~85:15, with a one-time index build spike in month 2 of ~50M embedding tokens.
2) Brightlyt prefers a single commercial ARR commitment (12-month) rather than tiered monthly iff there's an equivalent migration credit and an SLA commitment for latency/uptime during onboarding.

Can Redwood put an explicit warranty into the SOW for the migration milestones tied to the $100k credit and outline the SLA targets? Also — if you can show a worked example that lands us within 8–10% of current FluxScale full-year spend given the ramp above, procurement will likely greenlight a pilot.

Happy to set a Friday call (Apr 23) to walk through the numbers live.

Thanks,
Claire
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Claire Jenkins <cjenkins@brightlyt.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Vendor economics question — pricing match request

Claire — thanks for the detailed ramp. We reviewed internally and I can commit to the following commercial guardrails to get Brightlyt comfortably within the 10% TCO target stated you requested:

- 12-month ARR commitment SOW: we will structure a single ARR commitment matching the volume ramp you listed.
- Effective pricing after credits: gen $0.000545/token, embeddings $0.00082/token (worked example attached to the HubSpot deal).
- Migration assistance: $110k credit applied pro-rata across Q1 invoices plus a Statement of Work that defines the milestones to unlock each tranche; SLA clause for onboarding period (99.5% uptime; 95th pct latency objective) included.
- DocuSign: I'll route an initial term sheet once we lock the final volumes.

If that looks good, Sean — please send the HubSpot deal update and a DocuSign-ready term sheet. Claire / Tom — I can join the Fri call for any final executive sign-off.

—Karthik
